AzureOpenAI.//: NO LONGER an availability floor. The embedding model is now per-user (chosen in Settings — document RAG resolves its generator from the user's overlay, ADR 0007/0018), so EmbeddingDeploymentName is gone and nothing here is fatal-if-blank. Endpoint/ApiKey remain ONLY as the DORMANT Foundry-provider inheritance source (ProviderSettings.ResolveFoundry): baseline Models:Providers is empty (ADR 0019), so nothing reads them today; a user's Foundry provider declares its own endpoint + key. TenantId still binds DefaultAzureCredential for blob storage + ARM.
AzureOpenAI.//ApiKey: If ever set (for the dormant inheritance), it is a SECRET — never committed, arrives as AzureOpenAI__ApiKey. No longer required: the app boots with it blank/absent.

Models.//: Model providers (ADR 0013). A model is named by a QUALIFIED id, 'provider:model', split on the FIRST colon — GitHub's own ids contain a slash (openai/gpt-4o-mini), so a slash separator would have been ambiguous. An id with no colon is a legacy id and resolves against the default provider's namespace, which is why this needed no state migration.
Models.//Providers: EMPTY on purpose (ADR 0019): the app ships no baseline chat provider. Chat is entirely the per-user overlay (ADR 0018) — a signed-in user adds their own providers (Foundry, GitHub Models, Ollama, vLLM …) in Settings, each declaring its own endpoint + key. A user with none configured gets an empty picker and a gated composer. Do NOT add a provider here to 'seed a default' — that would reinstate the operator default the ADR removed.
Models.//Default: Stays "" (ADR 0019). There is no operator default model; the effective default is resolved per-user from the overlay (a user's pinned default, else their first declared model, else "").

WebSearch.//: The SearXNG sidecar in the same Container App. Containers in one Container App share a network namespace, so it is reached over localhost; 8888 because the backend's own ingress already owns 8080. Overridden by WebSearch__Endpoint in Bicep and by the AppHost locally.

Geocoding.//: Reverse geocoding for the get_current_location tool (ADR 0012). GoogleApiKey is a SECRET and is never committed: it arrives as Geocoding__GoogleApiKey, from a Container App secret in prod (GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY GitHub secret) or user secrets locally. Absent is a supported state — the tool then reports coordinates with no street address, and the app starts normally.

ContextScrape.//ApiKey: SECRET for the hosted context.dev page-scrape API behind fetch_web_page (ADR 0027). Never committed: it arrives as ContextScrape__ApiKey, from a Container App secret in prod (CONTEXT_API_KEY GitHub secret) or user secrets locally. Absent is a supported state and NOT on the availability path — the app starts normally and fetch_web_page fails per call, telling the model the page could not be read (unlike SEARXNG_SECRET, whose absence is fatal). The base address is config-pinned in code (ContextWebPageFetcher.DefaultBaseAddress).

Hindsight.//ApiKey: SECRET for the Hindsight long-term-memory service (ADR 0056). Never committed: it arrives as Hindsight__ApiKey, from a Container App secret in prod (the HINDSIGHT_API_KEY GitHub secret) or user secrets locally. Absent is the DEFAULT and a supported state, and it is NOT on the availability path: the app starts normally and BuildAgent attaches no memory provider at all, so a turn makes ZERO Hindsight calls rather than calls that quietly fail (the GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY shape, not SEARXNG_SECRET's).
Hindsight.//Consequence: SETTING this key is the decision worth pausing on, because there is no Settings toggle and no ToolCatalog key - not setting it is the ONLY off switch. Once set, EVERY non-incognito turn of EVERY conversation POSTs the user's message and the assistant's reply to a third party, and sends the user's message again as a recall query. That is broader than ADR 0013 (only when the user PICKS a third-party model) and ADR 0027 (only when the model CALLS fetch): it is automatic, always-on, and invisible in the UI. It carries whatever the conversation carries - document excerpts, the user's street address (ADR 0012), calendar content (now arriving over MCP, ADR 0063). Incognito chats (ADR 0034) are excluded, and so are image-generation turns; reminder and agent-run turns are INCLUDED, and those run with no user present.
Hindsight.//Mission: Optional bank mission, used to create each user's bank on first use. NOT a secret, which is why it lives here as a real committed value rather than arriving as a Container App secret like ApiKey does (the Push:PublicKey precedent). Empty is the default and means no create-bank call is ever made and the bank is assumed to exist; set it here and redeploy, or override with Hindsight__Mission, to have the bank created with a mission on first use. Deliberately NOT threaded through Bicep as a parameter: it is neither secret nor per-environment, so a committed default is the honest home for it.
Hindsight.//BaseAddress: Optional. Defaults to the Hindsight cloud (https://api.hindsight.vectorize.io); a self-hosted server is usually http://localhost:8888.

Diagnostics.//: Budgets for the live OpenTelemetry console at /logs (ADR 0054) — a bounded in-memory ring, no datastore, no secret, lost on restart. Nothing here is a secret and nothing is on the availability path: the section may be absent entirely (it IS absent offline, since tools/Agent42.DevHost has no appsettings.json at all) and each key falls back to its own default. MaxBufferBytes is the one that matters: the chat client runs with EnableSensitiveData=true, so a gen_ai span carries gen_ai.input.messages — the whole conversation serialised to JSON, on EVERY turn — plus every tool and skill schema in gen_ai.tool.definitions. Bounding by item count alone is an out-of-memory bug in a 1 GiB container that also hosts the SearXNG sidecar, so the ring is bounded by bytes as well, split evenly between the span and log rings, and a single oversize value is truncated (and marked) on the way in. MaxItemsPerPoll caps the /api/diagnostics response, which is otherwise unbounded per poll; a caller-supplied limit may narrow it, never raise it.
Diagnostics.//Logging: NOTE the Logs tab looks empty in production and that is CORRECT: Logging:LogLevel:Default above is Warning, and ILogger category filtering runs BEFORE the OpenTelemetry logging processor, so Information/Debug records never reach the buffer and no value here can recover them. The tab reports the effective minimum level for exactly this reason. Do not 'fix' it by lowering the level here — that changes what the app ships to the OTLP collector too. Raise it deliberately with Logging__LogLevel__Default if you need the verbosity.

Email.//: Inbound email (ADR 0096): mail sent to <agent token>@InboundDomain reaches a stored agent via a Mailgun Route forwarding to POST /api/email-in. InboundDomain is NOT secret. MailgunSigningKey (the account's HTTP webhook signing key) is the ONLY secret: it arrives as Email__MailgunSigningKey from a Container App secret in prod (MAILGUN_SIGNING_KEY GitHub secret) or user secrets locally. Without it the app starts, but /api/email-in answers 503 and accepts nothing. MANUAL PREREQS: MX for InboundDomain -> Mailgun (a SUBDOMAIN, never the apex), and a Route forwarding to https://chat.agent42.nl/api/email-in.

Push.//: Web Push notifications (ADR 0028) — a push titled with the agent's name when an agent replies on an async path (a fired reminder or an agent-run) while you're away. VapidPublicKey + VapidSubject are NOT secret and ARE committed here; the browser fetches the public key from GET /api/push/config. VapidPrivateKey is the ONLY secret: it arrives as Push__VapidPrivateKey, from a Container App secret in prod (VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY GitHub secret) or user secrets locally. Absent is a supported state and NOT on the availability path — the app starts, GET /api/push/config returns enabled:false, the UI hides the toggle, and no push is sent. MANUAL PREREQ: generate a P-256 VAPID keypair once (npx web-push generate-vapid-keys), paste the PUBLIC key below, and set the private key as the secret. Never rotate casually — a new private key invalidates every existing subscription.

Identity.//: Identity aliases (ADR 0074). Each entry maps an ADDITIONAL Entra object id (the KEY) onto the object id that OWNS the data (the VALUE), so one person holding two Entra accounts reaches one Agent42 dataset. Nothing is migrated: userId is the key for Cosmos grain keys, doc-chunks and chat-messages partition keys, blob prefixes and the Hindsight bank id, and Cosmos partition keys are immutable — so the incoming id is rewritten at the single choke point (CurrentUser.ResolveUserId) instead of the data being moved. NOT a secret: an Entra object id is an identifier, not a credential, and these are already committed in infra/main.bicep as the Easy Auth allowlist — which is deliberately what keeps this feature free of any Bicep, deploy-workflow or GitHub-secret change.
Identity.//DANGER: AN ENTRY HERE IS AN AUTHORIZATION GRANT, not a preference. The key is matched against the incoming X-MS-CLIENT-PRINCIPAL-ID and the value becomes that request's userId for EVERY durable store, so pointing a key at the wrong person both strands their own data and hands them the canonical user's conversations, RAG excerpts, street address (ADR 0012), Hindsight memory (ADR 0056 — no delete path) and share-link minting (ADR 0035). No validation can catch that; UserIdAliasTests only bounds it by cross-checking every id against authAllowedUserObjectIds in infra/main.bicep. NEVER name 'local-dev' on either side — that is CurrentUser's fallback for a request with NO Easy Auth principal header (the Dashboard:OwnerOid danger, in both directions); it is refused at bind time and pinned by a test.
Identity.//Rules: Validated at startup and DROPPED, never fatal — identity aliasing is not on the availability path. An entry is refused when either side is blank, when either side is 'local-dev', when it aliases an id to itself, when the value is not a bare hyphenated GUID (the value is concatenated into the grain key '{userId}/{conversationId}', which is split on the FIRST '/', and is a blob-path prefix), or when it forms a CHAIN or CYCLE — an id appearing as both a key and a value. Resolution is a single hop, so a chain is refused WHOLE, both entries, never half-applied. Two keys pointing at ONE value (fan-in) is legitimate and is kept: that is the three-accounts-one-person shape. Dropped entries are logged at Warning and counted in Settings -> Configuration.

Dashboard.//: The Orleans cluster dashboard at /dashboard (ADR 0062). Easy Auth already gates the path — it is absent from excludedPaths, which is default-deny (ADR 0002/0042) — and OwnerOid is a SECOND, narrower rule on top: of the users Easy Auth lets in, exactly one reaches the dashboard. That is what keeps a cluster console from becoming a third cross-user read surface beside /logs (ADR 0054) and /usage (ADR 0031), both of which show every user's data to any signed-in user.
Dashboard.//OwnerOid: The Entra OBJECT ID (a GUID) of the single permitted user. NOT a secret — an object id is an identifier, not a credential, and this repo is private — which is deliberately what keeps this feature free of any Bicep, deploy-workflow or GitHub-secret change. Find it in Azure Portal → Entra ID → Users → Object ID, or as a user.id attribute on any span in the production /logs console. FAILS CLOSED: blank or absent denies EVERYONE, so the dashboard is inert until this is filled in rather than open to every allowlisted user. Matched OrdinalIgnoreCase, so casing does not matter.
Dashboard.//DANGER: NEVER set this to "local-dev". That is CurrentUser.GetUserId's fallback for a request carrying no Easy Auth principal header, so configuring it here would hand the production dashboard to any unauthenticated request that reached the app. It is the correct value ONLY in tools/Agent42.DevHost and the AppHost, which have no Easy Auth in front of them — that is how one rule covers both environments with no IsDevelopment() branch.

Copilot.//: The copilot agent kind's runtime (ADR 0085). WorkspaceRoot is where each copilot chat's working directory lives: the Azure Files share in production (Copilot__WorkspaceRoot=/mnt/copilot, set by infra/modules/container-app.bicep), a temp directory when unset. Transcripts stay in the private 'copilot-sessions' Blob container either way.
Copilot.//BuiltInToolsEnabled: KILL SWITCH. Every copilot chat gets the runtime's built-in shell, file and URL tools INSIDE the backend container, auto-approved with no prompt, even on reminder and background turns (ADR 0107 amends ADR 0085). The shell runs as the app's user: it can read the container's files and every chat's workspace, reach localhost and the managed identity endpoint, and reach any host. false is ADR 0085's phase 1 (custom tools only, Mode.Empty). Restart after flipping it.

OAuth.//: The GitHub OAuth App behind 'Sign in with GitHub' (ADR 0108): copilot agents on the user's own GitHub Copilot subscription. An app identity, not an operator model (ADR 0019). ClientId is public; the secret comes from the GH_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET deploy secret (GitHub__OAuth__ClientSecret). Either blank: the GitHub Copilot provider isn't offered. Scopes stays empty unless the Step 0 check of the plan shows Copilot needs one.

Fleet.//: The agent fleet at /fleet/ (ADR 0097): recursive agent teams on the user's own models, run in-process (not in a grain) and persisted in the private 'agent-fleet' Blob container. Every task has a token cap: the page proposes DefaultMaxTokensPerTask, and the server refuses more than MaxTokensPerTaskLimit. Each user runs one task at a time, and MaxConcurrentTasks is the global ceiling. The other limits default to the engine's constants (see FleetOptions).
Fleet.//CopilotAgentsEnabled: KILL SWITCH. Copilot fleet agents keep Copilot's built-in shell, file-write and URL tools INSIDE the backend container (ADR 0097 amends ADR 0085 for the fleet only). Every write, command and fetch is asked to the user, but a shell can still read the container's files and reach localhost. false removes Copilot agents from the planner and refuses any YAML that asks for one.
